vocabulary._description: The grammar pin gate (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts) reports three counts for a lane, and this file uses the same three so the two documents can be compared directly. `ids` is tree-sitter's whole symbol space, which mixes three vocabularies; `namedUnique` and `anonUnique` are the two halves of it by tree-sitter's OWN nodeTypeIsNamed flag, not by a regex on the name. This spec buckets by ANALYZER REACHABILITY instead, which is a different axis and deliberately not the same partition — `internal_silent` holds named types (hidden `_rules`, generated `_repeatN`/`_tokenN` wrappers) AND anonymous tokens (punctuation, keywords, comments). The two axes are reconciled in `internal_silent.named_vs_anonymous`.

handled_verified._description: Analyzer-referenced node types, behavior-verified 2026-09-26 (real-css-analyzer.ts, at the CSS spec wave). Verification is three independent signals, all measured: 81 node types reached by a minimal reproduction (css-spec-classify.ts), 116 of 152 wasm symbol ids present in the real corpus of 185 non-empty svelte .css files (css-spec-corpus-census.ts), and for each type an observed symbol, edge, or pattern count. A type counts as HANDLED when the analyzer names it or reads its field AND it was observed in real code or in a reproduction — never on name alone. Handled does NOT mean "emits a symbol": the analyzer can handle a construct by consciously declaring that it emits nothing for it, and two types do exactly that (CSS-D5). The distinction that matters is handled vs unexamined: nothing in this list is merely unaccounted for. Types reached only through a parent construct (unit, integer_value, color_value, escape_sequence, feature_name, keyframe_block, binary_expression, …) are handled via that parent and are listed here rather than left unadjudicated.

flagged_anonymous._description: Handled, but tree-sitter's `nodeTypeIsNamed` flag says they are not named node types, so they are OUT of `types` above and would otherwise read to F3's section A as grammar drift. The flag is authoritative about the ABI and is wrong about intent here: `selector` is a rule of this grammar that the analyzer genuinely handles — `@media selector(.a)` reaches it — and tree-sitter reports it as a token because it is an alias target rather than a directly-declared named rule. Dropping the row would lose a real construct; claiming it as structural would be asserting something the wasm contradicts. It is filed here, in both directions.

internal_silent._description: Grammar-internal containers, generated repetition/token wrappers, hidden rules, punctuation and keyword tokens, comment and string payloads, and tree-sitter's id-0 end-of-input symbol — 72 of 152 unique type names across 152 wasm symbol ids (the id list repeats names, which is how tree-sitter aliases a token to several rules). Every entry below is silent BY CONTRACT: a symbol's edge names a construct, and none of these IS a construct. Each carries a stated reason so "silent" is auditable rather than assumed.

not_structural._description: Silent, and deliberately OUT of `types` above: the anonymous punctuation and keyword tokens, the hidden `_`-prefixed rules, the generated `_repeatN`/`_tokenN` wrappers, and tree-sitter's id-0 end-of-input symbol. None of these is a STRUCTURAL node type — F3's section A asks the grammar for `nodeTypeIsNamed(i)` with `_`-prefixed names dropped, and a row outside that vocabulary reads to it as grammar drift. They are silent for the same reason the rows above are silent, and the reasons are the same map.

named_vs_anonymous._note: tree-sitter nodeTypeIsNamed, from the census. The named half is entirely hidden rules, generated wrappers and comments; the anonymous half is punctuation and keywords.

limitations.scope: the .scss / .sass / .less files this lane is also ROUTED
limitations.severity: declared, not a defect in the CSS contract
limitations.measured: The product routes all four extensions to this analyzer (src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts lists .css/.scss/.sass, and script/m13/corpus-map.ts maps .scss/.sass/.less -> css), and every one of the 254 real .scss files in the corpus routes here — measured, 254/254. The CSS grammar does not support SCSS: 42 of 244 non-empty .scss files parse CLEAN (17.2%), 202 produce errors, 0 crash, for 11,451 distinct error lines. The lane still emits 4,477 symbols and 2,025 relationships from them, so a caller indexing an SCSS file gets a partial graph.
limitations.cause_breakdown: SCSS variables and @include dominate: $variable reference 17.9%, @include 12.8%, $variable declaration 6.7%, `//` line comment 2.7%, @use 1.6%, #{...} interpolation 1.2%, @each/@for/@if/@else 1.1%, @mixin 0.6%; 55.3% is the structural fallout of those rather than a separate cause. (@use looked like the dominant cause in a first pass and was not — that sample read only the first error rows of files in name order, and @use sorts early. The number above is every distinct error line.)
limitations.decision: DECLARED, and deliberately not fixed here. The plain-CSS rules inside an SCSS file parse correctly and are worth keeping, so removing the routing would take away real capability; and teaching the CSS grammar SCSS is a different grammar (tree-sitter-scss) with its own A/B, not a third hunk on a pinned 0.25.0 that has already been measured twice. What was missing was not the behaviour but the DECLARATION: nothing in the repo said this lane also receives .scss, so an 82.8% parse-failure rate on 254 real files was invisible to every gate. It is now stated here, in docs/analyzers/real-css-analyzer.md, and in reviews/m49-css-review.md.

limitations.measured: An IE filter value (`filter: progid:DXImageTransform.Microsoft.gradient(startColorStr = '#fff')`) does not parse. This is the same family as the relative-url defect that WAS patched, and it is the LARGEST remaining class by a wide margin: 37 of the 62 corpus .css files that still fail (60%), and in all 37 the error sits ON the progid line. It is not one class but two — 13 error files are genuine modern CSS the newest grammar cannot read (range queries, `&div`, `@page :right`, `[attr i]`, escaped unicode ids, HTML comments, `chrome://` imports, `--foo: ;`) and 37 are this one.
limitations.attempted_and_rejected: Adding `=` to the separator choice in the `arguments` rule — the obvious one-token edit — was built and A/B'd and is PROVABLY INERT: 61 error files before, 61 after, 0 fixed, 0 regressed, 151 -> 151 node types, 0 field delta. Not adopted, because adopting a build that changes nothing while looking like a fix is worse than not patching. The reason it cannot work is worth recording, because it is the opposite of the obvious diagnosis: the `progid:` TOKEN already lexes fine (`plain_value`'s trailing repeat has always admitted `:`), and the failure is INSIDE the parentheses. The value parses as `parenthesized_value`, whose rule is `seq('(', $._value, ')')` — exactly ONE value — so `startColorStr = '#fff'` cannot be a `parenthesized_value` at all, and `arguments` (which does allow separators) is unreachable because nothing matched the callee as a `function_name`.
limitations.decision: Left unpatched, and the reason is now measured rather than asserted. A real fix has to widen `parenthesized_value` from one value to a separated list, or add an IE-filter argument form — and `parenthesized_value` participates in EVERY parenthesized value in CSS (`calc((1px + 2px) * 3)`, nested parens, `var()` fallbacks). That is a different KIND of change from the two additive hunks adopted earlier, which only widened a token BODY and a step CHOICE while leaving every existing parse path untouched, and it would need its own A/B plus a shape-delta decision. Recorded so the next person does not write the inert patch: the cause is the rule's ARITY, not the token's character set.

limitations.measured: Both budgets are met (1.45 s over 2 files, 6.04 s over 185) but the run was measured at loadAvg1 31-37, and a row measured on a loaded box is not scored. The load-stable comparison is userCpuMsPerFile: 149.0 ms fixtures, 15.9 ms corpus.
limitations.decision: Left `unscorable` rather than re-run until the number happened to land. The gate's own rule is that a load-stable measurement is the only scorable one, and re-rolling until a host cooperates is how a red row becomes a green one without the code changing.

gap._description: EMPTY, and that is a claim with a method rather than a default. Searched for: a node type that parses with hasError=false and still yields no symbol, edge, or pattern. Two types parse clean and emit nothing by DESIGN and are recorded as rulings instead — charset_statement (an encoding declaration, not a construct) and universal_selector (* matches every element; publishing a symbol named * would be the same noise the HTML lane already ruled out for anonymous structural tags). Everything else that is silent is silent for a reason in internal_silent.reasons, and the earlier waves carry the behavioral half of this: the 41/41 M12 differential, the ontology class-resolution census, and the M59 line oracle over 7,647 edges.

design_decision.description: CSS contract rulings, each one reached by reading the pinned grammar and then MEASURED, because every one of them looked like dead grammar on the way in.

decisions.question: `end` is reported as node type id 0 by the wasm but appears nowhere in grammar.js or in the scanner's TokenType enum.
decisions.resolution: It is tree-sitter's end-of-input symbol, not a rule of this grammar — the language's reserved id 0, which is why enumerating node types reports it and why no source can ever produce it. internal_silent, with the absence from both grammars recorded as the evidence rather than a guess.

decisions.question: a `&`-composed nested rule's `contains` edge carries NO line, because the edge's TARGET is the RESOLVED selector (`.a { & .b {} }` -> `.a .b`) and that string is written nowhere in the file. 52 of the lane's 28,432 relationships are in this state. Should the line be omitted, or should it be the nested rule's own line?
decisions.resolution: OMITTED, on a measurement rather than a preference. Claiming the nested rule's line made 96 of 96 nested-selector edges INCONSISTENT against the source text — not because the line was nearly right, but because the name the line is supposed to carry is not in the file at all. The governing rule is M59's: a relationship's line belongs to the NAME node, not to the enclosing construct, and `.a .b` has no line because it is not written on one. The test for which case applies is not `does the selector contain &` — an IMPLICIT descendant (`.a { .b {} }`, no `&` at all) also resolves to a composed name that is written nowhere, and it accounted for the 67 INCONSISTENT edges left after the `&` test. The exact test is whether the resolved text and the as-written text are the same string, so the one case where the name genuinely IS written keeps its line. LOCATABILITY IS NOT LOST: the edge carries `asWrittenSelector` (`& .title`) in its metadata, so a consumer can find the site by text even though it cannot be given a line that would imply the name is there. The alternative — stamping the construct's line and weakening the oracle to check the as-written form instead — is defensible and was considered; it is not adopted because it would trade a guarantee the rest of the lane holds (the line carries the name) for one it does not (the line carries the construct), and that trade should be made once for the whole codebase rather than lane by lane.

decisions.question: the grammar defines postcss_statement (`at_keyword` + values + `;`) at prec(-1), but no reproduction reached it.
decisions.resolution: `at_rule` is un-precedenced and matches the same shape, so tree-sitter prefers it on every conflict: `@tailwind --apply;` parses CLEAN as at_rule + keyword_query, and `@custom-selector :--n .a, .b;` errors without ever producing postcss_statement. The analyzer therefore handles the construct through at_rule/keyword_query, which is the path real PostCSS-style directives take. Handling it as postcss_statement would have been a rule no input can select.

decisions.question: a named `important_value` rule exists alongside `important`; which one does real CSS produce?
decisions.resolution: `!important` produces `important`; `important_value` matches a non-standard `!foo` and is only ever produced INSIDE an error subtree — `.a { color: red !urgent; }` yields important_value together with hasError=true. A rule the analyzer can only meet on already-broken input is not coverage, so it is internal_silent with that measurement attached rather than counted as handled.

decisions.question: `of` is reported by the wasm but my first three candidate sources missed it entirely.
decisions.resolution: It is the anonymous keyword token of nth-child's selector list (grammar.js: `optional(seq('of', $._selector))` inside `pseudo_class_nth_child_arguments`), so the construct is the parent and the token is internal_silent. The reason it is a decision rather than a line in the reasons table: `.a:nth-child(odd of .b)` parses clean and produces it, while the more natural `.a:nth-child(2n of .b, .c)` spelling ERRORS in this grammar. Recorded because the obvious spelling is the broken one — a future reader must not 'fix' the reproduction into the form that does not parse.

decisions.question: the only two types that parse clean and emit nothing.
decisions.resolution: Both are silent by design, and both are in handled_verified rather than in gap BECAUSE the analyzer switches on them and decides: `@charset` declares the document encoding, which is not a construct a caller navigates to, and `*` matches every element — publishing a symbol named `*` would be the anonymous-structural-tag noise the HTML lane already ruled out. The measured count of clean-parses-with-no-emit types is exactly these two, and the search that produced it is recorded in gap._description. A zero-symbol result here is the contract working, not a gap.

decisions.question: two real value shapes the 185-file corpus never contains.
decisions.resolution: Reached by reproduction instead — `[full-start] minmax(1em, 1fr) [main] …` and `calc((1px + 2px) * 3)`, both clean. They are value payload under a property the analyzer already resolves, so no separate symbol is owed; the spec says so explicitly instead of letting corpus-absence read as ignorance of the feature.

decisions.question: the wasm id list is 151 long but only 129 unique type names appear.
decisions.resolution: tree-sitter assigns several symbol ids to one name when a token is aliased into different rules, so the census counts ids (151) and the spec counts unique names (129) and says so. Both numbers are stated in this file rather than reconciled silently, because a reader comparing 151 against 129 needs to know which is which.

decisions.question: 17 _repeatN/_tokenN wrappers and 6 hidden rules are unreachable by any source.
decisions.resolution: They are generated by tree-sitter's rule flattening and the external scanner: hidden rules are not named children, so no analyzer can receive them as a node, and the scanner's enum holds exactly DESCENDANT_OP, PSEUDO_CLASS_SELECTOR_COLON and ERROR_RECOVERY — the three that back real constructs. Recorded against the scanner source so the silence is a property of the grammar's shape, not of an omission in the analyzer.

decisions.question: three at-rules that wrap rules in a block, like @media and @layer do, but which the analyzer gives no symbol and no `contains` edge — so a rule inside one is published with no context at all.
decisions.resolution: Not a gap, and the reason is a property of the LANGUAGE rather than a choice about the analyzer: none of the three can be NAMED by anything else in CSS. There is no `var(@starting-style)`, no `@layer` that points at one, no query that resolves it — so a `contains` edge sourced from one would have to name a node that cannot exist, which is the unjoinable-string failure the F10 differential exists to catch. Compare `@layer base`, which another `@layer base { }` can join, and `@container card`, which a `container-name: card` can query: those two are nameable, so they get symbols and edges. The rules inside the three are still symbolized and their own declarations still read; what is dropped is the attribution that the language gives no way to express. NOTE these are not node types in this grammar at all — `@starting-style` reaches the analyzer as a generic `at_keyword` under `at_rule`, which is why they do not appear in `internal_silent` and why an earlier version of real-css-analyzer.ts pointed at a per-type entry here that did not and could not exist.

decisions.question: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts css css 0` reports 456,587 ambiguous + 4,883 unresolved of 485,882 edges. Is any of that ambiguity a defect the ANALYZER can fix, or is it the language's naming model meeting a gate that counts declarations?
decisions.resolution: RULED AS IRREDUCIBLE BY THE LANGUAGE, on a split measured with the arbiter's OWN counting rule (script/m14/incoming-rule.ts classifyEdge/tally, imported, not copied). The classification is asserted against the gate's own printed line at both scopes — the 60-file sample reproduces 32432/19291/12453/688 exactly, the whole population 485882/24412/456587/4883 exactly — so the split is of the number the gate reports and not of a lookalike. THE SPLIT: DUP-EMISSION 0 (no node published twice — the analyzer's own `ONE SYMBOL PER IDENTITY` merge, real-css-analyzer.ts:864-918, makes that structural); IN-FILE-MULTI 3, and those 3 are the only ones under ONE NAME AND TWO KINDS (`progress` published as a `type` rule and as a `function` keyframes in phoenix/installer/templates/phx_static/default.css) — which is exactly the gate's `amb(kind)` column reading 3 beside `amb(decl)` 456,587, the two-orders-of-magnitude gap its own header was written about; CROSS-FILE-ONLY 181 (1 in `imports`, 180 in `references`); CROSS-FILE-TWIN 456,403 = 99.96%, i.e. the edge's own file declares the target EXACTLY ONCE and every other declaration answering that name is in ANOTHER FILE (7,856 distinct targets over 516 files). WHAT THE BIG CLASS IS: 12,752 edges to `--pico-transition`, 9,460 to `--pico-color`, thousands to `--bulma-*` — Pico and Bulma ship 10-12 theme/variant builds, each of which really does declare the property, and the declaring files are not one file copied: the digest histogram over the same run puts only 1,178 of 456,587 edges on a target whose declaring files are all byte-identical, with the mass at 10-12 distinct digests. A CSS selector name or custom-property name is not an identity: `.nav` in two files is two real declarations that both apply, and the gate's question ('does this target name exactly ONE declaration') presupposes a 1:1 naming model the language does not have for these names. WHAT A FIX WOULD COST, measured rather than argued: the only file dimension the key space already contains is a symbol's `qualifiedName`, and respelling targets to it resolves 4,058 of 456,587 edges (0.9%) to exactly one declaration while 410,217 stay ambiguous and 42,312 have no such spelling at all — and for the `references` half it would assert a SCOPING the cascade does not guarantee (the analyzer classifies `var(--x)` as `import_based` precisely because the winning declaration depends on load order and specificity). The remaining option — a file-scoped published name for CSS selectors — is a family-wide publication-contract change (store `qualified_name`, parallel-indexer strategy 1, every consumer's idea of a CSS rule's name), not a lane fix, and it is not taken here. THIS RULING IS ABOUT THE AMBIGUITY COLUMN ONLY: the gate's verdict stays FAIL, because `bad` counts `ambiguousByDecl` and no claim mechanism can touch an edge whose target names a declaration.

decisions.question: 4,883 of 485,882 edges name nothing in their own project and carry no marker. Should this lane mark any of them external, or declare a cause?

counts.scope_split_command: npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts css css 0 — TABLE 1 (per project) unresolved 4883 vs TABLE 2 (pooled corpus) unresolved 4742

decisions.resolution: RULED: NO MARKER CAN VERIFY THESE, and the contract is read rather than guessed (script/m14/incoming-rule.ts). The dominant class is the CSS customization hook: `var(--fa-animation-duration)` in Font Awesome, `var(--pico-form-label-font-weight)` in Pico, `var(--bulma-*)` in Bulma — a stylesheet reading a property it deliberately does not declare, so the CONSUMER supplies it. That is genuinely external, and the marker is still the wrong instrument, because `verifyExternalClaim` (incoming-rule.ts:474) looks up `targetOwner` = everything before the LAST dot: `--fa-animation-duration` has NO dot, so the owner is null and the claim is `externalUnverified`; a Google-Fonts `@import` URL has `https://fonts.googleapis` as its owner, which carries `:` and `/`, also `externalUnverified`; the 46 `@primer/primitives/...` npm specifiers likewise. And `verdict()` (incoming-gate.ts:1159) requires `externalUnverified === 0` for a PASS, so marking converts `unresolved` into a different non-passing column — it buys nothing and spends the lane's credibility. The `cause` claim is worse than useless here: `baseBeyondRunScope` is REFUTED unless `base` IS the target's own owner, and a dotless target has no owner, so `causeRefuted` is counted AGAINST the lane (incoming-rule.ts:537-553). The 8 `dotted-name` imports (`e4_classic.css`) would verify, and are still not marked: a relative `@import` naming a file the project does not admit is a DANGLING INTERNAL reference, which the dart lane's own rule holds must not be excused with a marker, and the file claim that WOULD be the honest instrument (`importProjectFile`, checked against the project's admitted list) is REFUTED for them by construction — they are unresolved precisely because the file is not in that list. THE SCOPE SPLIT, the sharper form of external-vs-in-corpus: the gate prints TWO key spaces on one run, and 141 of the 4,883 targets are declared in ANOTHER repository of the corpus (unresolved per project, resolved or ambiguous pooled) while 4,742 are declared NOWHERE in the 1,174-file corpus at all. The first 141 are cross-project references, not externals; the second 4,742 are the external-or-dead mass, and no per-file analyzer can tell those two apart from inside one file. FLEET PRECEDENT, and it is the same finding twice: php records that 2,478 of its 2,483 unresolved targets have NO DOT AT ALL and that even a PERFECTLY marked php lane lands in `externalUnverified` and FAILS (docs/analyzers/real-php-analyzer.md:3279-3296), and fsharp rules that its 18,028 bare unresolved targets stay unclaimed and CANNOT be claimed, because a bare name has no owner, so marking one reads `externalUnverified`, which blocks a pass anyway (docs/analyzers/real-fsharp-analyzer.md:2422-2426). bash marks ONLY the narrow subset a LANGUAGE FACT proves cannot be a project declaration — a call whose command word contains `/` cannot be a shell function name — ten edges, zero refuted, pinned in both directions (docs/analyzers/bash.md:140-150). CSS has no such per-file fact for a custom property: ANY stylesheet may declare ANY custom property, so the claim is a PROJECT-level statement a per-file analyzer cannot support, and `verifyExternalClaim` cannot refute it either — an unfalsifiable marker is worse than a stated gap, so this lane writes none. The honest state is a reported, counted gap; the 14 `contains`/class-selector edges that were in this column BEFORE the chain-term kind fix (CSS-D13) are gone because they were a real defect, not because they were excused.

decisions.question: `resolves()` (real-css-analyzer.ts:822) admits a chain term through four sub-tests: the exact name, the dotted LEAF, any `:`/`.` boundary TAIL. The last two never asked what KIND of selector the published name is. Does that emit edges the corpus refutes?

counts.measured_case: contains ".button" -> ".button" [cssSpecific+isSelectorChain]; names.has(".button") = false; names.has("button") = true (a `button{overflow:visible}` type rule)

decisions.resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and the implementation is a KIND test rather than a deletion: a chain term is a single simple selector, so its spelling says which kind it is (`.x` class, `#x` id, `:x` pseudo, `*` universal, bare = tag/attribute), and a suffix match is now accepted only from a published name of the SAME kind (real-css-analyzer.ts `chainTermKind`). The exact-name test is untouched: a published name that IS the term is the term. THE DEFECT, measured before the change over the whole corpus: 29 chain edges withheld, of which 14 named nothing in their own project at all (the gate's `unresolved` column: `.button` in semantic.min.css, six `.small` and a `.h1` in bootstrap.css), 10 were ambiguous, and 5 the gate had called RESOLVED — the arbiter could not see those five, because a wrong target that happens to be unique looks exactly like a right one. Fixture `validation/m14/fixtures/css/chain-term-kind-must-match.css` was authored from the RULE before the change and FAILED against the unfixed analyzer on exactly its two forbid rows, with `.card -> .title` (both terms published class selectors) staying as the control that the fix did not simply stop emitting chains; after the fix all 21 css fixtures pass. THE SUFFIX SUB-TESTS ARE NOW MEASURABLY UNREACHABLE: over 1,174 files the census finds 5,912 chain edges and 11,824 ends, every one of them the exact name — leaf-only 0, boundary-only 0, unexplained 0, kind-inconsistent 0. The guard is retained (removing it would also strand `stripOccurrenceSuffix`, a helper the lane's provenance table documents) and its reachability is now a measured number rather than an assumption. RESIDUAL, reported and not fixed: 136 chain edges remain self-edges (`ul -> ul`, `.media -> .media`) and every one has both ends as exact published names, which is a repeated term in a real descendant selector rather than a fabricated pair — the lane's rule ('both chain leaves are published symbols') is satisfied, and suppressing them is a different question from the one this ruling answers.

decisions.question: A CSS name is not unique in its project: `.nav`, `--pico-color` and `fade` are declared in many files at once, so a bare-name target names N declarations and resolves to none of them. Production binds a bare name only when its count in the project is exactly 1 (`parallel-indexer.ts` strategy 2, `_res_name.cnt = 1`), and strategy 3 binds a DOTTED target to MIN(id) of the suffix matches — so a bare `--pico-color` binds to NOTHING and a bare `.btn` binds to an arbitrary file's rule. Should a target that names a declaration the edge's OWN file publishes be respelled to a project-unique qualified name? RULED: yes.

decisions.resolution: RULED — landed in src/ast/real-css-analyzer.ts, not attested. THE CAUSE, NAMED AND COUNTED FIRST. validation/m14/fixtures/css/ambiguity-classify.ts (counting rule imported from the arbiter, totals asserted against the gate's own printed line) splits the gate's 456,587 ambiguous edges: CROSS-FILE-TWIN 456,403 = 99.96%, CROSS-FILE-ONLY 181, IN-FILE-MULTI 3, DUP-EMISSION 0. CROSS-FILE-TWIN means the edge's own file declares the target EXACTLY ONCE and every other declaration of that name is in another file — so the language does not make the edge unresolvable; the published SPELLING did. WHAT IS PUBLISHED. Every symbol gains a project-unique `qualifiedName = <file-scope>::<name>`, where the scope is the file's path relative to its checkout root with the extension removed and `.`/`:` sanitised; an edge of type contains/references/uses/overrides is respelled to it only when the edge's own file publishes exactly one declaration of that name, and only when the longer spelling stays within the worker's budget. The bare spelling is kept for a name this file does not declare (a cross-file or external reference) and for `imports`, whose target is ANOTHER file's module — respelling it would point the import at the importing file. The symbol's `name` is untouched, and every rule can only ADD resolution. LOSSLESS, AND MEASURED. An A/B of the pre-change analyzer against the current one over the same 1,174-file population reads 487,744 edges for BOTH arms with delta 0 on every type. That matters because the shared filter `src/ast/pool-worker.ts filterNoiseRelationships` DELETES any target over 200 characters: without the budget guard 468 edges crossed it and were silently missing (the first run of this change read 485,414 against 487,744), so the rewrite refused to qualify a target that would cross it and left the bare name standing — until 2026-10-10, when the budget moved to the target's LEAF (`pool-worker.ts`, whose comment credits this lane's measurement as the reason), the guard was RETIRED and those edges resolved uniquely: the gate's `ofWhich` column went 1,883 -> 0 with the residual unchanged, i.e. 1,883 edges moved from resolved-by-tie-break to resolved-to-exactly-one-declaration. TWO SHARED RULES CONSTRAIN THE SPELLING, both asserted on live analyzer output by validation/m14/fixtures/css/qualified-target-compat.ts, whose controls MUST fire: (1) script/m14/differential.ts matches a truth row on `label + normTarget(target)` and normTarget takes the last `.`/`::` segment, so `::` with a dotless scope preserves the leaf the css differential compares (75 live qualified targets, 0 failures; the controls reject BOTH a one-colon separator and an extension-keeping scope); (2) the worker's LEAF budget, asserted by a control that KEEPS a 400-character scope with a short leaf and DROPS an 81-character leaf. WHAT REMAINS, NOT FOLDED INTO THE WIN. `references` keeps 180 ambiguous + 4,803 unresolved and `contains` 0 ambiguous + 0 unresolved under the gate; the 233 gate-ambiguous edges are `references` 180, `imports` 51 and `uses` 2 — none of them `contains`, whose collision-bound resolutions are now 0 — the 4,883 unresolved are the class this lane already classifies by marker set (4,803 dotless custom-property reads — the CSS customization hook — plus 80 imports), and a name declared twice in the edge's own file (3 edges) cannot be resolved by any file-scoped spelling because the edge does not say which site it means. extFAIL, bindFAIL and causeFAIL are 0 in both arms. TWO THINGS THIS RULING DOES NOT CLAIM. (a) The mandated run and the A/B disagree on the AFTER ambiguity — the gate reads 183, the A/B replication reads 2,066 — because the two build the project key space from different symbol sets (the gate's comes from parseFile, the replication's from the analyzer's own list). Both read ~95% before and ~1% after; the gate is the arbiter and is quoted as the headline, and the discrepancy is recorded here rather than averaged away. (b) The differential was NOT re-run at its pinned rotation: the normTarget identity, asserted on live targets, is the evidence that its comparison is unchanged, and a scoped run (rotation 1 of a cold pool, not the pinned sample) reported MISSING=2 on `imports` — a type CSS-D15 does not touch — and unexplained=1 on `overrides`, a label the harness itself prints as COMPARED WITH NO TRUTH. THE FIXTURES MOVED BECAUSE THE CONTRACT MOVED: 72 target assertions across 15 expectation files were re-spelled by the deterministic rule `<scope>::<name>` (not transcribed from analyzer output), each file carries a `_targetSpelling` note, and the suite reads 20 pass / 0 fail.

counts._resolution_note: RESOLVED IN TWO PARTS. (1) THE ARBITER WAS WIDENED (11fb2e07e, Lead's file): the dotless branch now tests `a spelling a published name may carry` instead of a JS identifier, with path/URI shapes still refused upstream by `pathLikeTarget` — the premise the old test rested on was already enforced before it. Its self-test carries ten assertions including both of this lane's cases (`--pico-color` declared -> refuted, `--pico-undeclared -> verified`). (2) THE MARKER IS ATTACHED in `real-css-analyzer.ts`, ONLY on a dotless `var(--x)` read that THIS FILE declares no property for — where the project declares it the edge resolves and the claim is never consulted, and claiming `external` for a name the file itself declares would be a false statement in the metadata even though no verdict reads it. Dotted custom-property names are deliberately NOT marked: `verifyExternalClaim` sends a dotted target down its OWNER branch, where a published owner REFUTES the claim, and `extFAIL` must stay 0. MEASURED: marked 5,641; `references` unresolved 4,803 -> 0; total residual 1.0% -> 0.1%; `extFAIL`/`bindFAIL`/`causeFAIL` 0; the 180 ambiguous untouched and `ofWhich` still 0. (3) THE STORE BINDING IS VERIFIED, which is the check that could have invalidated the whole of CSS-D15: a target carrying `:` is EXCLUDED from the bare-name resolution pass by construction, so a qualified target can only attach through the exact-`qualified_name` strategy. `validation/m14/fixtures/css/store-binding.ts` indexes a 120-file sample through `indexProjectParallel` (92 files, 50,578 symbols, 102,422 relationships) and reads `target_symbol_id` back: QUALIFIED 100,689/100,782 attached (99.9%), with `references` at 53,355/53,355 = 100.0%, against UNQUALIFIED 101/1,640 (6.2%). decisions.resolution: CROSS-TABBED, BOTH SIDES, AND THE CLAIM IS WITHHELD ON PURPOSE. TARGET SIDE: of the 5,641 dotless custom-property reads, 658 resolve in their own project (one declaration), 138 name a property declared ONLY in another corpus project, and 4,665 name one declared NOWHERE in the 1,174-file population; the remainder is exactly the gate's 180 ambiguous + 4,803 unresolved. So the claim would not be a lie about the population for the 4,665, and it would not be a name claim about a file (css has no business writing a `projectFile` claim for a property — that is the yaml counter-example's shape). VERIFIER SIDE, AND THIS IS THE BLOCKER: `verifyExternalClaim` (`script/m14/incoming-rule.ts:582-585`) handles a dotless target by asking about the TARGET ITSELF, but only when it matches `/^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$/` — a JS-identifier test. CSS targets are sigiled (`--x`, `.class`, `#id`), so all 5,641 read `externalUnverified`. The branch's stated premise is that `a path or URI cannot be a published symbol's name, so a lookup returning 0 would prove nothing about the claim`; for this lane that premise is FALSE — a custom property IS a published symbol name here (this analyzer publishes the declaration), so a lookup returning 0 proves the project declares no such property. The fourth control makes it undeniable that the test, not the marker, is what blocks: `--pico-color` reads `externalUnverified` whether or not the key space declares it, so a refusal there is not a safety property at all — it is the same verdict for a true and a false claim. WHY NO MARKER IS WRITTEN: attaching one today would move 4,803 edges from `unresolved` to `externalUnverified` — a different NON-PASSING column (`verdict()` requires `externalUnverified === 0`, which the gate's own header states is why the bare-name path was built for php and bash) — while asserting a fact a per-file analyzer cannot see and the arbiter cannot check. That is motion without progress on the one class the objective names, so it stays open and visible. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT, one line in the arbiter (Lead's file, not this lane's): widen the dotless branch from 'is a JS identifier' to 'is a spelling a published name may carry' — still refusing the path/URI shapes `pathLikeTarget` already catches and anything containing whitespace, but admitting the sigils. The gate's own controls at `incoming-gate.ts:1182-1194` already pin the bare-name path in three directions, so the widened test inherits a falsifier rather than needing a new one.

decisions.resolution: NARROWED AND PARTLY FALSIFIED — read this before the original text below, which is kept because the way it was wrong is instructive. The ruling below declined the candidate fix (resolving a relative specifier against the importing file's own directory) on the ground that it would GUESS a sibling whose admission a per-file analyzer cannot check, risking the 47 basenames that resolve for 51 it would often miss. That premise was then MEASURED by its own falsifier and it is FALSE: of the 106 basename-specifier imports, the 51 ambiguous ones have an ADMITTED sibling in 51 of 51 cases, and the 32 unique-basename ones with no admitted sibling do not exist on disk at all — so an existence-gated resolution fixes all 51 and risks ZERO of the edges that already resolve. The fix is landed (`siblingImportTarget`): imports 47 resolved / 51 ambiguous -> 98 resolved / 0 ambiguous, gate-measured over the whole `css,less` population. WHAT REMAINS RULED below is only the 80 unresolved. THE LESSON, which is why the old text stays: a ruling that names a mechanism as the obstacle must MEASURE the obstacle, not reason about it — this one reasoned, and the measurement reversed it. ORIGINAL TEXT: RULED, and the ruling is that NO CLAIM IS WRITTEN. The class is measured by shape: 46 basename specifiers RESOLVE (a file name that is unique in its project), 1 basename is ambiguous, and the remaining 80 are 46 npm/at-scope (`@primer/primitives/…`), 17 URLs (fonts.googleapis.com — `pathLikeTarget` refuses a URI by design), 9 bare names and 8 basenames the population does not carry. Each shape was checked against the claim kinds that could verify it, and none can: a file claim REFUTES on a miss (and these ARE misses), the project-facts verifier knows only `package:`/`dart:` spellings, and the owner verifier refuses a URI — returning `externalUnverified`, which `verdict()` counts against a PASS. So marking would be motion: the edges would move from `unresolved` to `ext?` and the lane would still not pass, while asserting an externality the arbiter cannot check. THE AMBIGUOUS 51 ARE ALL BASENAME COLLISIONS, and they are the `.less` half: 106 specifiers are bare basenames (55 `.css` + 51 `.less`), 51 of which name a basename that TWO OR MORE files in the project publish as a module — a basename is not an identity. The candidate fix (resolving a relative specifier against the importing file's own directory, the language's own rule) is declined on MEASUREMENT, not difficulty: every import here is a bare basename, an npm scope, a URL or a bare name, and NO path-carrying specifier exists at all, so the fix would have to guess a sibling whose admission a per-file analyzer cannot check — risking the 47 basenames that resolve today for 51 a guess would often miss. FALSIFIER, and the next measurement if this is reopened: count the basename imports whose SIBLING (`dir(importer)/specifier`) is itself an admitted file carrying a published module symbol. Near 51 means a real beneficiary and this ruling should be revisited; small means the guess trades resolved edges for unresolved ones. NOT MEASURED YET, and said so rather than assumed.
